content: {"rule":"K-S2","applies":"yes","applies_why":"The judge's UNDERDETERMINED ruling relies in part on the almah/bethulah word-count cutting both ways, so it decides whether ambiguous or double-sense wording may leave the link open, which is what K-S2 governs.","verdict":"BREACH","quote":"D5 vs C5 (Isaiah 7:14): UNDERDETERMINED -- the sign's chapter bounds (Isaiah 7:16; 8:3-4; 8:8) are real, but C5's own narrowing concedes Matthew 1:23's application stands, and the almah/bethulah word-count cuts both ways (Joel 1:8); answered in [CR2] section G and [CR3] LINK 5.","rule_words":"That a single verse does not state a link or its contrary is never a ground for STANDS or UNDERDETERMINED, for either side. A verse that carries two senses at once is not open. Both senses stand.","room":"The phrase 'cuts both ways' against the rule's 'carries two senses at once': I weighed (1) that 'cuts both ways' treats the almah/bethulah ambiguity as leaving the link open, which the rule forbids, against (2) that it merely reports mixed evidence without relying on a single verse's silence; I used reading (1).","why":"The judge uses the almah/bethulah word-count's cutting both ways as part of the reason for UNDERDETERMINED, which treats the two-sense/ambiguous evidence as open instead of letting both senses stand as K-S2 requires."}
